title: ISO 22301 Lead Implementer
summary: The ISO 22301 Lead Implementer is a professional certification for people who build and run a business continuity management system, which is the set of plans that keeps an organisation working during disruption. The programme sits at practitioner to manager level and is delivered by accredited training bodies rather than by the standards bodies themselves. It rewards candidates who already work in risk, resilience, operations or facilities management and who now want to prove they can set up the system, not just audit it. The exam is usually a written paper of multiple choice and scenario questions, and many providers also require a practical assignment in which you draft part of a continuity plan. It leads to roles such as business continuity manager, resilience officer, risk and compliance analyst, and information security officer with a continuity remit. The domain list below follows the published structure used by training providers, so check the current version with your provider before booking. This is an independent study guide and is not endorsed by any standards body or training provider.

beginner.definition: This is a professional certificate about ISO 22301, the international standard for business continuity. Business continuity means keeping the important parts of a company working when something goes badly wrong. The word implementer means you learn how to build that system, not how to inspect somebody else's.
beginner.whyItMatters: Companies lose money and trust when a fire, flood, cyber attack or power cut stops their work. This certificate shows an employer that you can plan for those days and lead the response. It fits people who already work in risk, operations or information security. It often helps you move from a technical job into a management or resilience role.
howItWorks: Learn the vocabulary of the standard first, such as business continuity, recovery time objective and management system.
Study the planning cycle in order, because the standard expects you to know how each step feeds the next one.
Practise on a real organisation, even a small one, and write down which services are critical and who owns them.
Draft the core documents yourself, including an impact analysis, a risk assessment and a continuity plan.
Test your draft plan in a table top exercise. Then explain what failed and how you would fix it.
Sit the exam, which mixes knowledge questions with scenario questions about an implementation project.
beginner.example: Think of a family bakery that loses power for two days. A careless owner waits for the lights to come back on. A careful owner knows the chilled stock must move to a neighbour's fridge within two hours. Two staff members hold spare keys, and customers can keep ordering by phone. The second owner did not stop the power cut, but kept almost all the income. A continuity plan is a written promise about what happens first, second and third.
takeaways: Continuity planning keeps services running during a crisis, while security work tries to stop the crisis.
You must read the standard itself, because the exam tests how well you understand its requirements.
Check with your chosen training provider whether the exam is a written paper, an assignment, or both.

objectives: Explain the purpose and structure of a business continuity management system
Plan an implementation project that fits the size, culture and risk appetite of a real organisation
Carry out a business impact analysis and record the recovery targets that come out of it
Select continuity strategies and solutions that can meet the agreed recovery targets
Run exercises that test plans and turn the lessons learned into improvements
Describe how internal audit, management review and corrective action keep the system alive

chapters.title: Business continuity fundamentals and the management system
objectives: Explain what a business continuity management system is and why a repeatable system beats a one-off plan
Describe how the standard is organised and how its main clauses fit together as a lifecycle
List the internal and external issues that shape how much continuity effort an organisation needs
Summarise the duties that top management carries under the standard, including the continuity policy
Outline a project plan with scope, milestones, resources and a communication approach
Describe how the project team is chosen and how its success will be measured

chapters.title: Understanding the organisation and setting the scope
objectives: Define the boundaries of the management system, including which sites, services and suppliers are covered
Document the legal, regulatory and contractual duties that affect continuity arrangements
Identify interested parties and explain what each one expects from the organisation during a disruption
Explain how the organisation's products and services depend on suppliers and third parties
Justify a scope decision to senior management and describe the risks of setting the scope too widely

chapters.title: Planning the management system
objectives: Write continuity objectives that are measurable and linked to the business strategy
Plan the activities needed to meet those objectives, with owners and completion dates
Describe how continuity responsibilities are documented and communicated across the organisation
Explain how continuity requirements are built into existing processes instead of being added as an extra task
Identify the resources, budget and skills the implementation will need

chapters.title: Supporting and running the management system
objectives: Determine the competence, awareness and training each continuity role requires
Control documented information so that plans are current, approved and easy to find in a crisis
Explain how internal and external communication is managed before, during and after a disruption
Describe the records that must be kept to show the system is working as intended

chapters.title: Business impact analysis, risk assessment and continuity solutions
objectives: Run a business impact analysis and record recovery time objectives and minimum service levels
Assess risks to the critical activities you identified and rank them using agreed criteria
Choose continuity strategies that match the required recovery time and recovery point
Write business continuity and incident response procedures that a tired person could follow at night
Define the resources, suppliers and premises that each chosen solution depends on

chapters.title: Exercising, monitoring and internal audit
objectives: Build an exercise programme that moves from discussion based tests to full rehearsals
Run an exercise and capture what worked, what failed and what must change
Define the monitoring and measurement that show whether continuity arrangements still meet their targets
Plan and conduct an internal audit of the management system
Track corrective actions from audit findings until they are closed and verified

chapters.title: Management review, certification and continual improvement
objectives: Prepare the inputs and expected outputs of a management review meeting
Explain how nonconformity is corrected and how the root cause is addressed
Describe how an organisation prepares for a third party certification audit
Summarise how continuity arrangements are updated after changes to people, systems or suppliers
